name: Socata Rallye
summary: French STOL-capable light single with an automatic-slatted wing. Easy to fly and used for touring, banner and glider towing; the forerunner of the TB series.

wings: Low cantilever wing with automatic leading-edge slats
engines: Single flat-four or flat-six in a short, blunt cowl
fuselage: Short, stubby fuselage with tall, upright cabin glazing
Fixed gear on short legs, mostly tricycle
tail: Conventional fin and rudder with a low-set horizontal tail

tellTales: Low wing with a slatted leading edge and big flaps
Short, stubby fuselage with a tall glazed cabin
Fixed tricycle gear on short legs

confusedWith.howToTell: The PA-28 has a plain unslatted wing and a long slab-sided fuselage; the Rallye has a slatted leading edge and a short, upright glazed cabin.
The AA-5 has a sliding bubble canopy; the Rallye has a tall, upright cabin glazing and a slatted wing.
The TB 9/10 is the later, rounder, humped-cabin design with no slats; the Rallye is boxier with slats on the wing.
